name: ai.ludo/game-assets
title: Ludo AI Game Assets
description: Generate game assets using AI: sprites, icons, backgrounds, 3D models (GLB) with auto-rigging (engine-ready joint naming), text-driven skeletal animation and curated animation-preset retargeting, animated spritesheets, videos, sound effects, music, and character voices. Supports multiple art styles including pixel art, low poly, and stylized 3D.

headers.name: Authorization
headers.description: API key from Ludo AI (format: 'ApiKey your-api-key'). Get your key at https://app.ludo.ai

examples.name: Generate Pixel Art Sprite
examples.description: Create a character sprite with specific art style
examples.note: createImage with image_type='sprite', art_style='16-Bit', perspective='Side-Scroll'

examples.name: Create Isometric Game Icon
examples.description: Generate an app icon for your game
examples.note: createImage with image_type='icon', perspective='Isometric', aspect_ratio='ar_1_1'

examples.name: Convert Sprite to 3D Model
examples.description: Transform a 2D sprite into a 3D GLB model with PBR textures
examples.note: create3DModel with texture_type='pbr' returns model_url (.glb) and 4 snapshot images

examples.name: Rig a 3D Model
examples.description: Add a skeleton to a GLB so it can be animated
examples.note: rigModel with model='<glb url>' and optional rig_type='humanoid' returns a rigged model_url (skeleton + skin weights baked in); run this before animate3DModel

examples.name: Animate a 3D Model
examples.description: Generate text-driven skeletal animations for a rigged model
examples.note: animate3DModel with model='<rigged glb url>' and prompt='walking' returns several candidate clips, each a standalone animation-only GLB plus an mp4 preview, to pick from and fuse onto your model. Rig the model first with rigModel

examples.name: Retarget an Animation Preset onto a 3D Model
examples.description: Apply a curated, hand-made animation clip to a rigged model
examples.note: animate3DModelPreset with model='<rigged glb url>' and preset_id from listAnimationPresets (only presets exposing a clip_url can be applied to a 3D model), plus optional crop_loop and in_place. Cheaper and more predictable than prompt-driven animate3DModel; requires a humanoid_template rig, so rig with rig_type='humanoid_template' or 'humanoid_template_hands' first

examples.name: Create Walking Animation
examples.description: Animate a character with a walk cycle
examples.note: animateSprite with motion_prompt='walking cycle', loop=true, frames=16

examples.name: Generate Attack VFX
examples.description: Create animated visual effects
examples.note: animateSprite with image_type='sprite-vfx', motion_prompt='fire explosion effect'

examples.name: Create Game Trailer Clip
examples.description: Generate a short video from a screenshot
examples.note: createVideo with duration=5, prompt='camera slowly zooms in'

examples.name: Generate Laser Sound
examples.description: Create a sci-fi weapon sound effect
examples.note: createSoundEffect with description='futuristic laser gun firing, sci-fi'

examples.name: Create Battle Music
examples.description: Generate background music for combat
examples.note: createMusic with description='epic orchestral battle theme, fast-paced, intense'

examples.name: Generate Character Voice
examples.description: Create a unique voice for a game character
examples.note: createVoice with voice_description='gruff old warrior', text='Prepare for battle!'

examples.name: Edit Image with AI
examples.description: Modify an existing image using text instructions
examples.note: editImage with image='url', prompt='remove the background and add clouds'

examples.name: Generate with Style Reference
examples.description: Create new content matching an existing art style
examples.note: generateWithStyle with style_image='url', prompt='a treasure chest', image_type='sprite'

examples.name: Generate Character Pose
examples.description: Create a new pose for animation preparation
examples.note: generatePose with image='url', pose='Attack Ready' - use BEFORE animateSprite for best results

examples.name: Rotate Sprite View
examples.description: Turn a sprite to a new camera angle, keeping the same pose
examples.note: rotateSprite with image='url', camera_rotation=90 (right side) and optional camera_elevation - generates directional/turnaround views

examples.name: List Animation Presets
examples.description: Browse available animation presets for motion transfer
examples.note: listAnimationPresets - returns animations, perspectives, and directions. Use preset_id + perspective + direction in transferMotion instead of a video URL

examples.name: Transfer Motion to Sprite
examples.description: Apply motion from a video or preset onto a different sprite
examples.note: transferMotion with image='sprite_url' and either video='video_url' or preset_id + perspective + direction - transfers animation onto a static sprite

examples.name: Control Animation Margins Per Axis
examples.description: Give wide animations room to move without wasting vertical space
examples.note: animateSprite or transferMotion with margin_ratio_mode='manual', margin_ratio_horizontal=0.4, margin_ratio_vertical=0.05 - ideal for sword slashes/punches (wide) or jumps (tall). Don't combine with the deprecated uniform margin_ratio

examples.name: Remove Image Background
examples.description: Remove the background from a sprite or image
examples.note: removeBackground with image='url' - returns a single transparent PNG

examples.name: Edit a Generated Spritesheet
examples.description: Re-prompt, outpaint, or fix the loop of a spritesheet you generated
examples.note: editSpritesheet with spritesheet_url='<url from animateSprite/transferMotion>' and edit_mode='prompt' + prompt='make the armor golden', or edit_mode='fix_loop' (no prompt) - the URL must be from your own generation in the last 7 days

examples.name: Compose Video from References
examples.description: Generate a video scene borrowing characters and style from up to 5 reference images
examples.note: createVideoFromReferences with prompt='the knight duels the dragon' and images=['url1','url2'] - optional aspect_ratio and eagle-audio model for a generated soundtrack

examples.name: Edit a Generated Video
examples.description: Modify a video you generated with a text instruction
examples.note: editVideo with video='<url from createVideo>' and prompt='make it night time, add rain' - optionally guide with reference images; the URL must be from your own generation in the last 7 days

examples.name: Upscale a Generated Video
examples.description: Double the resolution of a low-res video you generated
examples.note: upscaleVideo with video='<url from createVideo/createVideoFromReferences/editVideo>' - 2x upscale for videos below 960x960 pixels, flat 0.2 credits/sec; the URL must be from your own generation in the last 7 days

examples.name: Collect a Generation Result
examples.description: Pick up the asset from the job a generation tool returned
examples.note: Generation tools return {id, status:'queued'} immediately. Call getApiJob with that id, optionally wait=30 to long-poll (max 60), until status is 'succeeded' and read its result field, which is exactly the response documented for that tool. On 'failed' read error instead

examples.name: Manage Running Jobs
examples.description: See what is in flight and cancel work you no longer need
examples.note: listApiJobs returns your recent API/MCP jobs, filterable by a comma-separated status list (queued, running, succeeded, failed, canceled). cancelApiJob with a job id cancels a job that is still queued and refunds its credits; a job that already started cannot be canceled (409)

examples.name: Browse Generation History
examples.description: Search past generations from both the API and the web app
examples.note: listGenerations with type='spritesheet' and optional source='api'|'web'|'all', search='dwarf axe', request_id, date_from/date_to, page_size and page_number. Returns {items, page, page_size, has_more}; keep paging while has_more is true. It replaces the removed per-type results tools

notes: Credit-based pricing: images (0.5 each), 3D models (3), 3D model rigging (1), 3D model animation (0.2, returns multiple candidates), preset 3D animation retargeting (0.2), sprite animations (from 4, varies by duration/model), motion transfer (from 4, varies by duration/model), spritesheet edits (2/sec, min 4), reference videos (1.5-2/sec by model), video edits (2/sec), video upscaling (0.2/sec), videos (1 credit/sec on the standard model), audio: sound effects/ambiance (2), music/transform (3), voice/speech (1)
Supports multiple art styles: Pixel Art, Low Poly, Cartoonish, Stylized 3D, and more
3D models output as GLB with optional PBR textures

3D models can be auto-rigged (rigModel: adds a skeleton + skin weights) and then given text-driven skeletal animations (animate3DModel). Rig before animating. A model rigged with rig_type humanoid_template (or humanoid_template_hands) can also take curated animation presets via animate3DModelPreset, using a preset_id from listAnimationPresets. animate3DModel returns several candidate clips, each a standalone animation-only GLB (skeleton + one clip, no mesh) plus an mp4 preview, for the caller to pick from and fuse onto the model in their engine/three.js
Spritesheets support variable frame counts (4-64) and sizes (64-256px)
Long-running operations (3D models, animations) may take 60-120 seconds

Generations run on a job queue. Over MCP every generation tool is asynchronous: it returns {id, status:'queued'} immediately and the result is collected with getApiJob (pass wait up to 60 seconds to long-poll). Non-terminal responses carry poll_after_ms. There is no async parameter on the MCP tools

On the REST API the same queue is driven by an async payload flag: synchronous stays the default until September 10, 2026, after which requests default to async and return 202 with a job id. Setting async: false keeps synchronous behavior during and after the transition

Job tools are free: getApiJob (status/result, optional wait long-poll), listApiJobs (recent API/MCP jobs, filter by status, limit capped at 100), cancelApiJob (cancels a still-queued job and refunds its credits)

listGenerations is the free, paginated generation history across both surfaces: filter by type, by source (api|web|all), by free-text search, by request_id or by date. It replaces the removed per-type results tools (getImageResults, getSpriteResults, getVideoResults, getAudioResults, get3DModelResults), which are deprecated in the REST API

Fair use: up to 50 generations queued or running per account (further submissions return 429 with code PENDING_JOBS_LIMIT), and 150 requests per 5 minutes per API key on the read endpoints (job status, job listing, generation history); a 429 carries Retry-After

All generated asset URLs are temporary Google Cloud Storage links that expire after 7 days: download and save assets locally (or re-upload to permanent storage) before they expire, especially anything destined for production use; never store the returned URLs as permanent references
